newsitem.title: USA: HCC Insurance eyes more acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: HCC Insurance eyes more acquisitions.

text.p: HCC Insurance Holdings Inc is eyeing more acquisitions in its push to become the biggest writer of general aviation insurance in the United States, Chairman and Chief Executive Stephen Way said.

The Houston-based international specialty insurance group consolidated its general aviation business with the recent acquisitions of Fredricksburg, Md.-based AVEMCO Corp and Continental Aviation Underwriters Inc of Memphis, Tenn.
The deals follow other recently completed acquisitions and bolster the company's worldwide general aviation premium income to about $225 million, Way told Reuters in a recent interview.
"We're going to expand the aviation side a bit more, and we're also expanding our accident and health side with more acquisitions," Way said.
The likely time frame is "sooner rather than later," Way said. He declined to elaborate.
HCC is spreading its general aviation wings after a six-year absence from the U.S. market. Way said the business became too competitive in 1991, "and nobody's made any money in that period of time."
General aviation is a specialty line that excludes insurance for airlines and satellites.

HCC feels the depressed industry cycle will turn up soon. "We sensed that the bottom might be coming and we wanted to pick a time to get in at the bottom of the market, before it started up again, and maybe to help it along, if we could," Way said.
"Not to be arrogant that our involvement would change the face of the business, but if we could do it substantially enough, then we would certainly have an effect on it."
HCC will try to restore realistic pricing to the U.S. general aviation market, Way said.

"What we want to do is through being the biggest, is set the leadership role in getting the business more profitable. If it backfires, other people will be too competitive and they'll take our business, and hopefully they'll lose a lot of money."
Way said HCC would pitch its pricing to make a profit, "not to squeeze huge amounts of profit out of the public, but just to break even as a start, because this business has not been profitable."

"I don't think the competitors who are left are not going to take the chance to increase their rates, because they know they're losing money, and they just haven't had the opportunity to change it," he said.

"We're going to set the trend, and see if they follow. If they don't, we're prepared to lose business. We're not going to write business at an underwriting loss. If you look at our history, in 16 years we've never had an underwriting loss in the entire company."

Way said that the wave of consolidation sweeping the worldwide insurance industry will inevitably affect specialty lines like general aviation. He said this is why HCC bought a direct writer like AVEMCO to complement its four agency companies including Houston Casualty Co.
"Consolidation is going on throughout the industry, and in our little specialty areas, there's no reason consolidation couldn't work there too," he said.

"We have a philosophy that there isn't too much capacity in the world, it's just that too many people have it. If you consolidate the number of people, it doesn't matter if the capacity's still the same, as long as less people control it. Therefore, it should become more responsible."
